doc.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: White artists covering R&B hits
summary: Pat Boone and others covered rhythm and blues hits with better distribution; Plas played on Ricky Nelson's Fats Domino cover.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Oh, no. There was many, but I don’t know. I don’t have any idea which was first. There was a period where the white artists were kind of covering these rhythm & blues records that were coming out and if they made any kind of radio noise and you could tell it was going to be a hit, well they would cover it maybe with their own artists and superior distribution and everything and just take the hit away.

Yeah, Pat Boone started doing a Fats Domino thing. Well that’s taking the hit one step higher, because I’m sure he could sell so many more records on that. And young Ricky Nelson, I played on his stuff, and he did some Fats Domino, “I’m Walking.”
